basic_identification.full_title: Specification for Electric Cables for Aircraft — Part 3: Nyvin Type Cables
basic_identification.sector_category: Electrotechnical / Aircraft Electrical (approved by the Electrotechnical Division Council and finalized by the Aircraft Electrical Sectional Committee of the Bureau of Indian Standards)

scope.summary: This standard (Part 3) specifies the requirements and tests for Nyvin and Uninyvinal type electrical cables used for aircraft wiring. These cables are suitable for use in circuits where the voltage between conductors, between a conductor and a metal braid, or between a conductor and the aircraft structure does not exceed 600 Vrms and the frequency does not exceed 1600 Hz. They are suitable for continuous operation where no combination of ambient temperature and conductor current produces a stabilized conductor temperature exceeding 105°C, and are suitable for fixed installations in aircraft up to 75°C, but are not suitable for severe flexing at low temperatures.

certification_and_marking.standard_type: Product Specification / Type & Acceptance Tests (Aircraft Electrical Hardware)
certification_and_marking.certification_status: Voluntary Certification Scheme (ISI Mark). Under the provisions of the Bureau of Indian Standards Act, 1986, manufacturers of aircraft electrical cables are eligible to obtain a license to use the Standard Mark (ISI Mark) on coils, reels, or drums. This certificate acts as an assurance of rigorous quality compliance under continuous BIS checks. Precious metal hallmarking is completely inapplicable to electrical insulation and wire cores.

requirements.detail: Each coil, reel, or drum of certified aircraft cable may carry the BIS Standard Mark (ISI Mark) to verify manufacturing quality and trace compliance.
Measured conductor resistance per 1000 meters of finished cable must not exceed standard limits for copper and aluminium (with aluminium resistance limits ranging between 127.0 to 169.0 ohms).
Cables categorized as Uninyvin 22 to Uninyvin 12 must be protected with an outer concentric nylon sheath to prevent fluid and mechanical abrasion.
Uninyvin sizes 10 to 0000 and all Uninyvinal cables must feature an outer protective covering of nylon braid (or braided nylon ribbon) coated with a clear nylon lacquer.

All core insulation colors must remain completely fast to light and moisture during prolonged storage. Cables must have their nomenclature permanently printed in red (for Nyvin) or black (for Nyvinal), separated by spaces of 150 to 300 mm.
The glass braid lay factor is strictly controlled by cable size: a) Sizes 22 to 18: 1.5; b) Size 16: 2.0; c) Size 14: 2.25; d) Size 12 and larger: 3.0.
Specimens must withstand air oven ageing at 120 ± 2°C for 120 hours, cooled within 1 hour, removed from the mandrel, straightened, and subjected to subsequent electrical checks to detect cracks.

Prepared specimens must be immersed in a 5 percent aqueous sodium chloride solution at 20-25°C for five minutes with insulation protruding 38 mm. An AC voltage potential at 25 to 100 Hz must be applied between the conductor and liquid.
Immersed cable specimens must withstand a test voltage of 1500 Vrms for one minute between the conductor and water without suffering dielectric breakdown.

requirements.requirement_type: Spark and Core Spark Test Limits
requirements.detail: Spark testing of core insulation specifies a potential of 3 kV (rms) up to and including size 6, a core test voltage of 1500 Vrms, and a 500 V dc spark test with minimum insulation resistance requirements.
The PVC insulation compound must be tested per IS 5831:1984. Retained tensile strength and elongation at break after heat ageing must be at least 90 percent of the unaged baseline values.

Specimens must undergo a 28-day tropical exposure conditioning test (incorporating mold growth tests per Part 10 of the environmental testing code) and then survive a 1500 Vrms voltage test with minimum insulation resistance equivalent to 4.57 M ohm for 1000 m.

plain_language_summary.summary: IS 10241 (Part 3) : 1987 (Reaffirmed 2014) is the national Indian Standard specification governing 'Nyvin' and 'Uninyvinal' type insulated electrical cables used for aircraft wiring and aerospace outfitting. Prepared by the Aircraft Electrical Sectional Committee (ETDC 55), it defines the material, dimensional, and rigorous safety-testing criteria for cables rated for circuits up to 600 Vrms and frequencies up to 1600 Hz. The standard dictates the application of concentric nylon sheaths or lacquer-coated nylon braids for environmental protection, specifies strict lay factors for core glass braiding, and mandates a series of severe physical and electrical tests—including 120-hour heat ageing at 120°C, 28-day tropical mold-growth exposure, 5% salt-water dielectric testing, and a 1500 V high-voltage water immersion test—to ensure zero electrical failures under extreme flight conditions.
